invariant_rationale: Owned and borrowed array-copy markers deliberately carry different transfer invariants despite their identical zero-data enum shape.
C and C++ parameter directions belong to independently versioned generated metadata schemas and are converted at the binding boundary.
C ABI and C++ native blocking policies describe different generated contracts and remain nominally distinct across their boundary.
Protocol and lifecycle scenario evidence occupy separate report fields whose nominal types prevent cross-category benchmark attribution.
Call count memory and time keys select different test instrumentation tables and cannot be substituted across measurement dimensions.
Local and meta tracing keys select different production instrumentation tables and cannot be substituted across trace ownership domains.
C and C++ metadata producer identities belong to distinct generated manifest schemas and are converted only by package tooling.
Publication URLs, yank arguments, support bundles, and SQL capabilities expose separate failure contracts whose nominal wrappers prevent cross-domain error substitution.
The managed-image A-CHAMP node owns actor-heap references while the VM map node owns persistent host-side entry indexes.
Support bundle and accelerator commands parse distinct CLI schemas while JSON invocation arguments borrow native resource values with operation-specific lifetimes.
Repository quality internals use textual errors while standalone quality executables preserve typed boundary failures and convert explicitly at their interface.
CUDA availability and Tokio feature auditing use deliberately narrow Cargo manifest projections with different required fields.
HIR diagnostics retain source-model context while type-check diagnostics retain inference and constraint context before rendering.
The available and unavailable libpq pollers are mutually exclusive target implementations of one cfg-selected adapter surface.
The HIR callable signature is a language contract while the specialization signature is a local NativeIR cache key.
The syntax attribute preserves Terlan source expressions while the renderer attribute owns sanitized output-ready HTML values.
Syntax attribute values retain expressions and spreads while renderer values are normalized text or boolean output values.
The syntax element preserves parser spans and expressions while the rendered element owns output-tree structure.
The syntax node is compiler input and the renderer node is sanitized output so conversion is intentionally explicit.
The pull-request proof inventory and full proof-track inventory deserialize different checked TSV schemas.
The metadata enum is serialized capability identity while the runtime struct owns live dispatch state and resources.
The compiler test dispatch signature models emitted calls while the runtime dispatch signature models admitted native execution.
Compiler syntax signatures are semantic declarations while emitted metadata signatures are serialized artifact records.
List and A-CHAMP node headers encode different actor-heap layouts and are never layout-compatible.
Aggregate-projection origins track call provenance while termination origins track recursive proof provenance.
Lean replay metadata is quality evidence while NativeBoundary replay metadata is runtime correlation data with explicit conversion.

Package-owned HTTP and EPMD requests have separate protocol contracts; VM storage requests retain backend authority and pending actor state while decoded storage-worker requests contain only validated operation payloads; PostgreSQL requests retain database operation arguments and result contracts.
Mutually exclusive Unix and Windows platform modules name the native polling source RawSource; RawFd and RawSocket preserve their respective operating-system handle widths and ownership contracts.
Each server guard owns teardown for a different process harness and cannot safely stop another harness type.
HIR trait method signatures preserve declarations while type-check signatures own resolved generic and conformance state.
The in-process and capability-required workers are mutually exclusive cfg-selected implementations of one VM-owned interface.
Artifact budgets reserve staging bytes and leased generations, interface budgets bound parsed source keys and idle time, and storage budgets charge actor-owned resources and retained bytes.

Disk retention entries track persistent byte usage, parse entries own shared syntax results, proof admission entries bind tool contracts to executable identities, and multicore inventory entries describe invariant evidence rather than cached values.

Build operations classify emission accounting, binary and string pattern operations decode different versioned instruction formats, and storage operations retain lifecycle completion projections; these types are not interchangeable representations.
The LSP backend owns editor client state while the storage backend owns a capability-worker event pump and deadlines, with independent lifetimes and authority.
Proof regression policy sets measurement thresholds, storage policy selects durability modes, and resource worker policy binds host capabilities and transport failure contracts.

Distributed-state resources retain conflict-resolution values and in-memory entries, while storage resources retain encoded checkpoints, adapters, and lifecycle proofs in a separate actor-owned registry. PostgreSQL worker resources own live connections and rows while VM database resources hold fenced worker handles; scheduling resources own placement and recovery state.
Storage adapters retain durable authority, PostgreSQL adapters retain database resources, and generic resource adapters retain owner-checked remote handles with distinct lifecycle rules.
Cloud deployment arguments identify a remote release and idempotency scope while experimental deployment arguments select local planning actions and parse failures.
Storage pending work owns commit uncertainty while database and generic resource pending work retain different reply projections and worker ownership contracts.
Native boundary errors classify resource and ABI failures while WebSocket errors classify transport progress and connection closure for socket polling.
Database reply projections preserve PostgreSQL operation semantics while generic resource projections bind package operation contracts and owner-checked remote handles.
PostgreSQL worker results own database response values while HTTP descriptor results alias validated source descriptor conversion failures at the host boundary.
Managed value materialization tasks retain allocation traversal state while value hashing tasks retain ordered hash traversal state without allocating managed objects.
SSE wire records validate event limits and keep-alive intervals while WebSocket wire records validate frame limits, binary policy, and channel pairing.
Database worker registries own PostgreSQL connection processes while generic resource worker registries enforce host-selected capability policies and package resource lifetimes.
The production WebSocket hub owns rooms and peer lifecycle state while the test-only shared unit handle cannot admit peers or represent production state.
Release discovery owns a bounded GitHub API client while WebSocket clients own transport connections and frame lifecycles.
Source route descriptors retain evaluated fields before admission while routing records contain validated paths and ordered execution callbacks.
Source router descriptors describe evaluated declarations while admitted routers enforce unambiguous dispatch and executable middleware ordering.
Source route targets retain descriptor values while admitted targets carry validated channel plans or executable handler callbacks.
